candidates.lead: Jawad Ali has spoken out on the issue after capturing a racist outburst in footage shared widely online
candidates.evidence_text: Doorman who witnessed racist outburst says abuse 'becoming normal' - BBC News Image caption, Jawad Ali, 20, said he now expects racial abuse when he goes to work By Kaya Black North West Published 1 hour ago A doorman who shared a video of a racist outburst he witnessed while at work has said such abuse towards staff is becoming "normalised". The footage, taken outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, showed a woman shouting abuse and making gestures at a black security guard. Jawad Ali said the club-goer became abusive after being asked to move away from an exit while he was working at the venue on Saturday night. Greater Manchester Police said it had received a report about the incident and inquiries were ongoing. Image caption, Footage of the incident has been shared widely online "It's disgusting," said Jawad, 20, who was working for Protective One Security at the time. He alleged the woman had also directed racial abuse towards him before the filming. Jawad said he decided to post the video on social media because "you can't do that and get away with it". "This isn't the first time, and it won't be the last," he added. Jawad said during the past two years working on the doors he has been called every racial slur and even threatened with death. "I expect now when I come to work to be racially abused one night out of the four that I work," he continued. "Its a normal thing now. It should be a big thing that gets prosecuted heavily." Image caption, The incident happened outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale Fellow security worker Liz Turley, who works for Radius Security, said: "There hasn't been a night where I haven't experienced some instance of somebody standing there for a prolonged period of time giving me abuse." She said staff were often subjected to racist, homophobic or sexist abuse on shift. "They will pick up on characteristics that we're likely to find offensive," she added. Jawad told the BBC he believed that online discourse about immigration issues had emboldened racist attitudes, particularly with narratives around "stopping the boats". "We haven't come off any boats. I was born here, my dad was born here, my granddad was born here," he said. "I've got just as much right to be here and work as anyone else does." Liz said she would like to see members of the public to stand up for others when they see these instances taking place. "Very often these individuals are left unchallenged in committing this sort of abuse," she said. candidates.summary: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: concrete_story_change:declared. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
candidates.evidence_text: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss - BBC News Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October By Naj Modak , North West and Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said. Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport. Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas". He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk". As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning. The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs. In Salford, 41 properties were targeted with three in Tameside and two in Stockport over the period. Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Windows are seen boarded up on one property due to concerns of further attacks According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti. On Tuesday the window on one of the properties was smashed. Neither of the properties in Heaton Norris were currently used as HMOs, despite claims on social media. One is understood to be for sale while the owners of the property where the windows were smashed were asking Stockport Council for permission to convert it into an eight bedroom HMO. One of the owners, who wanted to remain anonymous, said he was planning to house young professionals if planning permission was approved. The vandalism and criminal damage follows similar incidents in Salford where suspected HMOs were targeted. Police said evidence suggests the attacked were linked to the criminal exploitation of children with a 13-year-old boy previously arrested. Image source, MEN Image caption, There are fears the violence has been fuelled by influencers on social media Noden said the force recognised that the spread of damage to properties across Greater Manchester would be worrying for residents. Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester , he said specially trained officers were looking into social media posts being circulated. To those on social media encouraging the attacked, Noden, said: "Stop what you are doing - lives are being put in danger". "I want to reiterate that we are taking this spate of damage extremely seriously and are continuing to relentlessly target offenders, including those who we believe are using and exploiting children to orchestrate the criminality," he said. Two men, aged 46 and 39 were also arrested on Monday for the same offence and released on bail. He said, "I hope it sends a strong message that anyone involved in this offending will be made to answer for their actions". Anyone with information that could support the investigation is being asked to contact the police. candidates.evidence_text: Sinkhole revealed 50 metre deep mine shaft uneder road - BBC News Image caption, A sinkhole found in March revealed a 50m deep sinkhole By Kevin Fitzpatrick and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 21 October 2026 Work is taking place to repair a sinkhole which revealed a 50m (164ft) mine shaft under a busy road in east Manchester. Part of the northbound carriageway on Alan Turing Way has been closed since March, when the road surface began to sink. Since then, Manchester City Council has filled the hole with more than 100 tonnes of concrete. It said it expected the route to be open again December. Image caption, Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin says it has been a "massive job" Mandie Shilton Godwin, the executive member for transport, said it had been a "massive job", adding it had "taken an awfully long time”. She added: "It started in March when the depression was noticed, but it wasn't until the end of September when the team were absolutely sure what the problem was. "Once they were sure what the problem was, then they could begin to put it right. "No one could have anticipated the scale of the void that we found but, once it became apparent, all of our effort went into making sure the site was safe and the road could be reopened." A concrete cap is currently being put over the mine shaft. Work will then need to take place to fill the remaining void beneath the road, and lay a new surface. candidates.evidence_text: Three more arrests in Alisha Samuels murder investigation - BBC News Image source, Family photo Image caption, Alisha Samuels was found dead following a disturbance in the Newton Heath area By Rebecca Brahde North West Published 21 October 2026 Three more arrests have been made in connection with the suspected murder of a woman who was stabbed in a street in Manchester. Alisha Samuels, 26, was found dead after officers were called to a disturbance on Dorking Avenue in the Newton Heath area of the city at about 02:00 BST on Thursday. On Tuesday, Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, was charged with the murder of Samuels and the attempted murder of a man. Earlier two men, both 19, were arrested on suspicion of murder and a 48-year-old woman was held on suspicion of assisting an offender, Greater Manchester Police said. Det Ch Insp Justin Bryant said: "We remain focused on establishing the full circumstances and want to reassure Alisha's loved ones that we are committed to securing justice for her. "My thoughts remain with Alisha's family and friends as they continue to come to terms with this devastating loss." The detective renewed an appeal for witnesses or anyone with information to come forward. candidates.lead: Wigan Council said it had listened and "struck the right balance" between supporting growth and creating jobs
candidates.evidence_text: Wigan council 'listening' as warehouse plans dropped - BBC News Image source, Joanna Allsop Image caption, Members of the Save Our Astley and Boothstown Greenbelt at a summer protest By Kevin Fitzpatrick North West Published 21 October 2026 A consultation is due to end on Wigan Council's plan for future development, with four sites potentially earmarked for warehouses being removed. It follows an outcry from residents over the construction of huge warehouses close to homes near Astley. The local authority said it had listened and "struck the right balance between supporting economic growth and job creation". Greenbelt campaigners and opposition councillors claimed they had forced the council to act. Councils must put together a local plan which identifies sites for housing and business development every decade or so and Wigan is in the process of updating its own. In the version under consultation, it has said four sites would not be taken forward. They include to the north of M6 junction 26, Moss Industrial Estate extension, Bridgewater West in Astley, and West of Winwick Lane in Lowton. The site being described as Bridgewater West is known locally as Higher Green and more than half a million sqaure feet of employment space was to have been built. Joanna Allsop from the Save Our Astley and Boothstown Greenbelt lives nearby and said; "It was just unbelievable that anyone could suggest that it could be anything other than Greenbelt." She said they are still concerned about its future, adding: "What we want is long-lasting protection. We want them to say that it is Greenbelt, not try to say that it's Greybelt." 'Fiasco' The changes follow anger over the Astley warehouses which have led Mayor Bev Craig to question why modern industrial developments are being allowed so close to residential properties. Wigan Council's Labour leader, Councillor Nazia Rehman, said; "I would say some lessons have been learned, consultation will be proactive when it comes to communities and how they want their places changed and what type of developments they want to see in their area. "So we are working wherever we can to try to consult deeply when it comes to our communities." Leader of the opposition in Wigan, Reform UK Councillor Paul Watson said: "If there is one positive outcome from the Astley warehouse fiasco, it is that all the four additional commercial warehouse sites in the borough have been removed from the 2040 plan." The consultation ends at 17:00 BST on Wednesday 21st October 2026. candidates.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said there had been 25 attacks across Salford on houses thought to be HMOs since 5 October with most "racially or religiously motivated" The Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said there were fears the attacks on HMOs suspected of housing migrants had been fuelled by far-right influencers who had posted videos of the homes on social media Salford City Council's planning lead Mike McCusker said: "There's been a set-up that's led to this

P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. candidates.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

He flew from Manchester Airport to Cancun with his partner Michelle for a 10-day holiday on Isla Holbox - an island off the northern coast of Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula - earlier this year It included four days of tarpon fishing in the picturesque Gulf of Mexico on a special flat-bottomed boat. Steve said the final day of fishing was dramatically cut short after another boat ploughed into theirs He said he was casting his rod into the waters around two miles from the shoreline when the crash happened at around 7.30am. Steve said a boat on the horizon seemed 'quite a bit bigger', carrying around a dozen tourists. It was heading 'straight towards' them, he added

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Murder accused said 'he's under the car' after hitting Stretford Grammar headteacher, trial told by cousin who was in Volvo Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work Add to preferred sources News Amy Wal The cousin of the man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins told jurors the defendant knew the tragic cyclist was under his car as he was dragged to his death while she watched from the passenger seat Gabrielle Debotte, who was in Simon Richardson's Volvo, said he told her 'he's under the car' before she heard 'moaning' from beneath the car. Mr Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:37, 21 Oct 2026 New details have been released on Bury council’s savings plans after town hall bosses warned ‘distasteful’ decisions have to be made The local authority is facing a difficult financial situation, with a £20m budget gap identified for the coming financial year if no action is taken. Bosses believe they have identified a way to reduce that gap to around £9.6m through a number of cost cutting and revenue raising The measures have previously been described as ‘regrettable’ and ‘distasteful’ by finance lead Sean Thorpe. However, ‘all options’ have to be considered, he said These include measures around garden waste, street lighting, social care payments, school crossing patrols and leisure charges. The authority had also been considering cuts to youth services, but has now said it will not be doing this after finding an alternative way to fund them The authority’s executive last week signed off on entering into conversations with the Government over Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to help bridge the remaining gap. EFS allows town halls greater flexibility when it comes to meeting expenses

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Everything you need to know as Oldham council by-election to take place Six candidates are running with voters going to the polls next month Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 14:58, 21 Oct 2026 View I Six candidates are running in the battle to win a key seat in an Oldham town next month On November 12, voters across parts of Failsworth will be going to the polls to choose their next councillor. The by-election was called after Mark Wilkinson, the former leader of Reform UK in the borough, stood down for health reasons Reform Oldham saw widespread success at the May local election, propelling the party’s presence from a fringe group to the second biggest in Oldham council. The Failsworth West ward, which is being contested, was represented by three of the party’s councillors before Mr Wilkinson The upcoming by-election could be a key test for Reform UK following ‘personal and demeaning attacks’ on social media while for Labour , it will be a test of whether Prime Minister Andy Burnham is winning back voters. The election is also against the backdrop of the council’s ong The upcoming by-election will see Reform looking to hold onto the seat and fend off Restore Britain. For Labour, it will be a test of whether Prime Minister Andy Burnham is winning back voters following May’s devastating result for the party in Oldham

The holidaymakers, who paid up to £3,000 each, claim they encountered an 'overp They said they raised concerns about hygiene in buffet restaurants where flies could be seen around uncovered food. P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Appeal was being launched in Manchester today ahead of Remembrance Sunday next month. And this year's launch will involve four specially created poppies - each one crafted from the metal of iconic Second World War RAF Spitfire fighter planes The launch of the Royal British Legion's appeal marks the start of the national period of remembrance, when the nation wears the red poppy to remember the service and sacrifice of armed forces personnel. All funds raised will be used by the legion to support veterans and their fa The poppy became a symbol of remembrance and hope for a peaceful future in the aftermath of the First World War. The 2026 appeal aims to raise £50m

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

candidates.evidence_text: Homelessness Manchester homeless charity serving 32,000 meals a year issues plea for support from business community Coffee4Craig offers a free hot meals and other essential services from its Cheetham Hill base Add to preferred sources Comments News G A Manchester homeless charity which served more than 30,000 warm meals last year is seeking fundraising support as its running costs reaching £30k a month alone Coffee4Craig has been running since 2013, when Risha Lancaster and her husband Hendrix founded the charity following the death of Risha's brother Craig “The day I discovered Craig had died, I posted on Facebook ‘If you see someone sleeping on the streets, buy them a coffee and say it was from Craig – and from then the charity took off,” said Risha The charity offers free warm meals to the homeless from their site in Cheetham Hill every evening, providing a home-cooked meal, pudding, tea and coffee for two hours, and further 'relief and recovery' programmes during the day. Between June and October this year they served almo "It gives people a bit of dignity and no judgement, they get to know people and get to trust people," Risha said. candidates.lead: Courts Murder accused said 'he's under the car' after hitting Stretford Grammar headteacher, trial told by cousin who was in Volvo Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work Add to preferred sources News Amy Wal The cousin of the man accuse
candidates.evidence_text: Courts Murder accused said 'he's under the car' after hitting Stretford Grammar headteacher, trial told by cousin who was in Volvo Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work Add to preferred sources News Amy Wal The cousin of the man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins told jurors the defendant knew the tragic cyclist was under his car as he was dragged to his death while she watched from the passenger seat Gabrielle Debotte, who was in Simon Richardson's Volvo, said he told her 'he's under the car' before she heard 'moaning' from beneath the car. Mr Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:37, 21 Oct 2026 New details have been released on Bury council’s savings plans after town hall bosses warned ‘distasteful’ decisions have to be made The local authority is facing a difficult financial situation, with a £20m budget gap identified for the coming financial year if no action is taken. Bosses believe they have identified a way to reduce that gap to around £9.6m through a number of cost cutting and revenue raising The measures have previously been described as ‘regrettable’ and ‘distasteful’ by finance lead Sean Thorpe. However, ‘all options’ have to be considered, he said These include measures around garden waste, street lighting, social care payments, school crossing patrols and leisure charges. The authority had also been considering cuts to youth services, but has now said it will not be doing this after finding an alternative way to fund them The authority’s executive last week signed off on entering into conversations with the Government over Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to help bridge the remaining gap. EFS allows town halls greater flexibility when it comes to meeting expenses

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Three more arrests made after woman, 26, stabbed to death in Newton Heath A 26-year-old man has previously been charged with the murder of Alisha Samuels Add to preferred sources News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 12:46, 21 Oct 2026 Updated 07:3 Greater Manchester Police have made three more arrests in relation to a woman who was stabbed to death in Newton Heath Officers were called to a 'disturbance' on Dorking Avenue in the early hours of Thursday (October 15) where 26-year-old Alisha Samuels was sadly pronounced dead at the scene On Tuesday (October 20) GMP said that Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue in Manchester, has been charged with her murder and the attempted murder of a man, and remanded in custody ahead of a magistrates' court appearance Today (October 21), the force confirmed that three more people had been arrested in relation to her death, with support from firearms officers and the Force Critical Wanted Unit Two 19-year-old men have been arrested on suspicion of murder, while a 48-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. They remain in custody for questioning

Mr Richardson didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors allege, while Mr Mullins wa He was dragged along the road for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors at Minshull Street Crown Court previously heard that Mr Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April this year. The 56-year-old headteacher was cycling home to Northwich after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, the c Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins from underneath the vehicle. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - or 1.3 miles Earlier in the trial, witnesses described seeing the Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane. Mr Richardson denies murder, an alternate offence of manslaughter and dangerous driving, and is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crow Footage has been released on Wednesday morning, October 21, showing the moments before Mr Richardson was arrested after a period of alleged dangerous driving on April 21. The dashcam footage, which was shown to the jury on Tuesday afternoon, October 20, shows Mr Richardson allege He is then seen to brake sharply in the middle of the road before fleeing from the drivers side Yesterday, jurors heard evidence from officer in the case DS Tricia Solomon, who confirmed that the last time the Volvo was driven by Mr Richardson was the night before, April 20, before it was swapped for a silver van. The Volvo was said to be of ‘obvious interest’ to the police

It is the place where they fe Trafford families have been left ‘heartbroken’ and ‘devastated’ after the closure of one of the borough’s primary schools was approved by the council Government rules say local authority funded schools can only carry a deficit for three years , while Trafford council allows for five years in ‘exceptional circumstances’ and if there is a plan to bring it back to a balanced position. St Teresa’s reported its first year of losses The council has argued there are more than enough pupil places in the north of the borough to take the pupils who will be displaced by the closure. But parents told the Local Democracy Reporting Service their fight to save the school was about ‘so much more than a building’ View 4 Images St Teresa's RC Primary School, St Teresa's Road, Stretford (Image: Google) Helen Fitzpatrick’s two daughters have attended the school , with her eldest Anais moving on to secondary school this academic year and Delilah now in Year Four. Ms Fitzpatrick said opposition to the closure was about ‘fighting for our children’s wellbeing , the teachers' future

candidates.evidence_text: Travel 'Our £3k Mediterranean cruise was meant to be a celebration, it turned into a nightmare' A number of women from Greater Manchester, who paid up to £3,000 each, fell seriously ill onboard the P&O ship Add to preferred sources News Ed Chatterton A group of passengers from Greater Manchester who booked a P&O cruise to celebrate a 60th birthday say their trip turned into a 'nightmare' after they fell seriously ill onboard The group, some from Bolton, Bury and Wigan, were struck down with gastric illness and flu-like symptoms while travelling around the Greek islands on the P&O Azura between May 28 and June 4 this year. The holidaymakers, who paid up to £3,000 each, claim they encountered an 'overp They said they raised concerns about hygiene in buffet restaurants where flies could be seen around uncovered food. Many were left confined to their cabins during the eight-night trip, while others were hospitalised when they returned back to the UK The group have now instructed international injury lawyers to investigate their illnesses. P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. She said the illness left her battling a catalogue of health problems

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

He flew from Manchester Airport to Cancun with his partner Michelle for a 10-day holiday on Isla Holbox - an island off the northern coast of Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula - earlier this year It included four days of tarpon fishing in the picturesque Gulf of Mexico on a special flat-bottomed boat. candidates.lead: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Com
candidates.evidence_text: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:37, 21 Oct 2026 New details have been released on Bury council’s savings plans after town hall bosses warned ‘distasteful’ decisions have to be made The local authority is facing a difficult financial situation, with a £20m budget gap identified for the coming financial year if no action is taken. Bosses believe they have identified a way to reduce that gap to around £9.6m through a number of cost cutting and revenue raising The measures have previously been described as ‘regrettable’ and ‘distasteful’ by finance lead Sean Thorpe. However, ‘all options’ have to be considered, he said These include measures around garden waste, street lighting, social care payments, school crossing patrols and leisure charges. The authority had also been considering cuts to youth services, but has now said it will not be doing this after finding an alternative way to fund them The authority’s executive last week signed off on entering into conversations with the Government over Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to help bridge the remaining gap. EFS allows town halls greater flexibility when it comes to meeting expenses

candidates.evidence_text: National news LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 15 hours ago Stretford Grammar headteacher murder trial RECAP after court hears driver 'smirked' at passenger, who heard 'moaning' under car Simon Richardson denies murder and is on trial at Minshull Street Crown Simon Richardson is alleged to have murdered Mr Mullins after running him over as he cycled home before dragging him under his car for more than a mile. The 35-year-old didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors allege, while Mr Mullins was trapped under the car He was dragged along the road for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Last week jurors at Minshull Street Crown Court heard Mr Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April this year. The 56-year-old head cycling home to Northwich after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, the court was told Simon Richardson driving moments after the collision with visible damage to the bonnet of the car Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins from underneath the vehicle. He then got back behind the wheel and turned sharply in a bid to 'remove' Mr Mullins before he carried on driving, veer

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Paramedic's horror as motorbike turns into fireball just months after importing it from China Kian Gregory's motorbike caught on fire at his residential tower block in Salford Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Wri A 25-year-old student paramedic has urged other motorcyclists to be wary when importing vehicles from abroad - after his burst into flames just two months after buying it Kian Gregory, who lives in Salford and relies on his motorbike to get to work, said the bike caught fire just hours after he returned home from a shift with the ambulance service. He had parked the machine in the compound at the bottom of his tower block at around 10pm By approximately 5.40am, it had been destroyed in a fire. The blaze was spotted by a neighbour heading to the bins, who alerted the fire service Speaking to the Manchester Evening News, Ki an said: “The bike has essentially self-combusted." He had owned the bike for just two months, he said.. The vehicle had covered around 2,500 miles and, according to Kian, had been meticulously maintained by its previous owner, and was imported from China

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 21 October 2026 at 6:20pm Four children died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home in Salford in 2017, their mother died two years later after suffering severe burns. Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in “great danger” days before Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is ongoing at Bolton Coroners’ Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told that on November 29, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: “The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger.”

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

Credit: Studio Egret West A little under a year after the city council signed off the redevelopment of Albert Bridge House into 800 apartments and 250,000 sq ft of workspace, a formal decision notice has now been issued Having signed a Section 106 agreement with Manchester City Council, Oval Real Estate is now armed with planning permission to demolish the modernist Bridge Street office block and build two residential towers of 37 and 49 storeys and a 17-storey office As is standard for schemes in Manchester that cite viability as a constraint to delivering on-site affordable homes, Oval’s S106 contains a viability clawback mechanism. This means that the scheme’s viability will be reassessed at a later date to see if contributions up to a maxi While now in possession of a decision notice, Oval could still be a way off starting on site. Given the scale of the scheme, the developer will have to secure Gateway 2 approval from the Building Safety Regulator before work can begin The scheme sits just outside the Kendals district being developed by Relentless Developments, Gary Neville’s property company

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

candidates.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.evidence_text: What began as a one-room osteopathy clinic in Hale has evolved into something much more specialised Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Martin and Sabrina Machata, co-owners of ProSpinal in Hale What began as a one-room osteopathy clinic in Hale has evolved into something much more specialised. Six years on, Martin and Sabrina Machata have unveiled ProSpinal – combining hands-on For Martin and Sabrina Machata, changing the name of their Hale clinic from Fern Clinic to ProSpinal was about much more than a new sign above the door What began in 2020 as a traditional, one-room osteopathy practice has evolved into a specialist clinic increasingly helping people with persistent back and neck pain, disc injuries, sciatica, trapped nerves and arthritis – including patients who have already tried other treatment At its new home at The Stables on Ashley Road, ProSpinal combines the hands-on osteopathy on which the business was founded with innovative technologies including IDD Therapy, MBST, Shockwave and TECAR “We are still, at heart, osteopaths,” says Martin. “We’re still helping the general public with all sorts of aches and pains. But we also have the speciality of helping patients who have non-resolving back pain and neck pain.”

Six years on, Martin and Sabrina Machata have unveiled ProSpinal – combining hands-on For Martin and Sabrina Machata, changing the name of their Hale clinic from Fern Clinic to ProSpinal was about much more than a new sign above the door What began in 2020 as a traditional, one-room osteopathy practice has evolved into a specialist clinic increasingly helping people with persistent back and neck pain, disc injuries, sciatica, trapped nerves and arthritis – including patients who have already tried other treatment At its new home at The Stables on Ashley Road, ProSpinal combines the hands-on osteopathy on which the business was founded with innovative technologies including IDD Therapy, MBST, Shockwave and TECAR “We are still, at heart, osteopaths,” says Martin. “We’re still helping the general public with all sorts of aches and pains. But we also have the speciality of helping patients who have non-resolving back pain and neck pain.”

candidates.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

candidates.evidence_text: A passenger in a car that dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile has told a murder trial the driver could hear the victim from inside the vehicle after hitting him Gabrielle Debotte said she "still had visions" of the moment her cousin, Simon Richardson, hit 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins at 18:07 BST on 20 April before driving away Giving evidence from behind a screen, Ms Debotte told Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that Richardson spent the night after the crash "laughing and joking" and drinking alcohol Richardson, 35, denies murder and an alternative count of manslaughter The jury heard Mr Mullins was trapped under the vehicle and dragged 2.2km (1.3 miles) The married father-of-two was found injured by a motorcyclist who had followed a trail of blood from near the crash site on Paddock Lane to Wet Gate Lane. candidates.lead: A report going to the Council’s Executive committee this week (Weds 14 October) charts record numbers of affordable homes being delivered in wards across Manchester to meet city-wide demand
candidates.evidence_text: A report going to the Council’s Executive committee this week (Weds 14 October) charts record numbers of affordable homes being delivered in wards across Manchester to meet city-wide demand Data broken down by Council ward shows how affordable housing investment in communities – particularly in north and east Manchester and Wythenshawe – is helping to meet an ambitious target to help deliver at least 10,000 social rent, Council and genuinely affordable homes up to 2 Now nearly halfway through the Housing Strategy period from 2022, when combining affordable completions with developments on site and alongside housing in the future pipeline, the city is already close to securing development to meet the 10,000-home target Taken alone, major affordable development both completed and planned for Miles Platting and Newton Heath (1,289 homes), Cheetham (1,070 homes) and Ancoats and Beswick (806 homes) shows a healthy pipeline of projects in communities with high demand for affordable housing Substantial regeneration programmes will also further bolster the city’s housing investment outlook, with key schemes in Holt Town and Strangeways still to come online, while further significant housing investment is continuing at Victoria North and in our District Centres across In the last year, Manchester City Council reported record numbers of completions where 4,766 homes of all types and tenures were finished – contributing to the Housing Strategy target to build 36,000 homes up to 2032

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements These measures are designed to strengthen democratic oversight, provide clear political leadership across key service areas and support transparent decision-making while the borough continues to work towards the appointment of a Council Leader and Cabinet The arrangements were approved by Council on 16 September and include the creation of interim Lead Member and Deputy Lead Member roles aligned to the Council's four directorates The arrangements form part of a wider governance framework developed following legal advice, engagement with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and discussions between political group leaders. candidates.evidence_text: Experience Bolton’s FREE winter light art festival and enjoy four unforgettable nights of spectacular illuminated installations, captivating performances, and immersive experiences for all ages Curated in partnership by Bolton Council and Things That Go On Things, Put Big Light On Festival will run from Thursday 19 November to Sunday 22 November across Bolton town centre, between 5pm and 9pm every day With illuminated installations, roaming performers, and larger-than-life creations, the festival will showcase a mix of contemporary outdoor arts and family-friendly performances designed to surprise and delight audiences At the heart of this year’s festival, the Loom of Light by dbnAudile will take inspiration from Bolton’s textile heritage to transform Victoria Square into a mesmerising and striking walk-through artwork Using illuminated threads of light and colour to create an evolving structure that visitors can explore from within, this showstopping and interactive feature offers a contemporary interpretation of the weaving traditions that helped shape the town’s textile history Stretching across the square, the installation promises a memorable visual experience, with glowing strands of light creating a dramatic backdrop for photographs, exploration, and discovery throughout the festival

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council’s Income Maximisation team has helped residents across the borough secure almost £30 million in additional financial support over the past three years, making a significant difference to thousands of households The team supports residents to access benefits and financial assistance they may not realise they are entitled to, helping to boost household income, ease financial pressures and improve overall wellbeing The Income Maximisation team plays a key role in the council’s Here For You campaign, which was launched during the cost of living crisis to provide free, confidential advice, and practical support to help residents access the assistance available to them Among those who have benefited from this service are Lowton residents Cynthia and Jonathan, who described the support they received as having made 'a massive difference' to their lives Cynthia said: “We’ve got pensions and didn’t have much savings, but we never thought that we were entitled to anything “We were just amazed and couldn’t believe what we were entitled to. It feels like you’ve got to tap yourself, because it’s such a weight off like you wouldn’t believe.”

Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . evidence_packet.evidence_text: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The untold story of the rebellious middle child of Emmeline Pankhurst takes centre stage in this irresistible hip hop, funk and soul musical that moves your feet and fires your spirit. Whilst her mother and sister battled for women's suffrage, Sylvia ignited a revolution for the forgotten: working women, the impoverished, the silenced. Caught between her family and her beliefs, Sylvia risked it all to bring change to millions. With an electrifying score by Josh Cohen and DJ Walde , renowned choreographer and storyteller Kate Prince (ZooNation - Message in a Bottle, Some Like it Hip Hop, Into the Hoods, The Mad Hatter’s Tea Party ) delivers her Olivier-nominated vision in this theatrical treat that audiences can’t get enough of. Starring powerhouse talent Beverley Knight , ( Sister Act, The Drifters Girl, Memphis the Musical ) in a show stopping performance as Emmeline Pankhurst, this is your chance see her in a career defining turn that won her the Olivier Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role. Naomi Katiyo ( Hamilton, Just For One Day: The Live Aid Musical ) stars as Sylvia Pankhurst, a role that brings depth, heart, and fire to the stage. Direct from London’s Old Vic theatre where it played to sold out houses and instant standing ovations, SYLVIA is more than a musical – it's a manifesto set to music, a revolution you can dance to, a story that roars and shakes the rafters. It can feel busy and overwhelming without much clarity on what’s actually working. This programme is about helping people step back, put the right foundations in plac The Monthly Marketing Programme is delivered through a structured monthly format, with immediate access to a starter guide on sign-up. candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: The event will bring together more than 20 venues for cocktail takeovers, tastings, collaborations and special events Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Manchester is getting a brand new dedicated cocktail festival this November, with a week-long programme of events taking place across some of the city’s best-known bars Manchester Cocktail Festival will run from Monday 9 to Sunday 15 November, bringing together more than 20 venues for guest bartender appearances, special cocktail menus, tastings, dining experiences and industry events The festival has been created by Nick Coupland of Liar’s Group, the hospitality company behind Crazy Pedro’s, Cane & Grain and Science + Industry, alongside Ben Kendrick of Speak In Code and Double Down Inspired by similar festivals in other UK cities, the pair hope to celebrate Manchester’s cocktail scene while creating opportunities for collaboration between bars, drinks brands and hospitality professionals Participating venues include Speak In Code, Blinker, The Morris, Winsome, Bar Shrimp, Double Down, Stray, Bar Dos, Crazy Pedro’s and Hawksmoor, alongside Northern Quarter favourites Science + Industry, The Daisy and The Bay Horse Tavern

At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

The interior showcases the works The famous cocktail menu will return, featuring favourites like the Pink Picante, Pomme Verte – a popular twist on an appletini, Belfast Coffee, the famous spicy pickle martini Especiado and the Pornstar Chic, crafted with homemade passionfruit sorbet Red Light also introduces a brand-new savoury snack menu, including, Boquerones, Pickled Guindilla peppers, Gordal olives, Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade Salted Popcorn Ice Cream. To complement the elevated look and taste, Red Light has curated energetic, “Red Light has always been about bringing people together over exceptional drinks in an inviting, unpretentious environment. Our new location gives us the space to realise that vision fully, with the same soul and now a proper home for cocktails, food, and great music.”

candidates.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

Along with a special reissue of the record, Texas have unveiled a brand-new single Another Way To Cry , which you can listen to below “It didn’t feel risky because no one at our label gave a shit,” Spiteri recalls of the attitude towards the band in the UK ahead of White On Blonde . “We were in Glasgow, we made the album in my house and I did all the vocals in the coat cupboard. Four-legged family members can also join the fun with the return of Bark Hütte, a pup-sized hütte wi Alongside karaoke, the pop-up’s popular wreath-making workshops will return. Priced at £55 per person, including a glass of fizz or mulled wine, classes will be running on Sun 29 Nov (2pm-4pm) and Tue 1 Dec (6.30pm) Perfect for families, Bae Huttë’s Santa Claus Club is back, too. Enjoy an hour of karaoke with a free hot chocolate per child (up to six children) and colouring pads for the kids. Plus, there’ll be an opportunity to grab a selfie with Father Christmas himself on Sun 13 Dec and Su Booking is strongly advised, but walk-ins are also welcome. There will also be plenty of outdoor seating available under a heated stretched tent, giving Christmas partygoers the chance to get merry without getting cold

candidates.evidence_text: A moonlit community run which aims to empower women and girls to stay active and enjoy outdoor exercise through the winter months comes to Platt Fields Park this week Organised by Manchester Parks in partnership with the running community, the welcoming and inclusive event is not just for experienced runners but for people just getting started and who are looking to become more active, helping them connect with local walking or running groups The event offers a chance to meet local run clubs, find new running partners and pick up tips to run safely through the darker months. Taking place on Thu 22 Oct from 6pm-9pm, the event is open to all genders and abilities, but organisers hope that it will be particularly helpful The first event earlier this year saw 210 people take part to complete a 3k run or walk around the park in a series of waves. Some of the more experienced runners even completed all seven waves and bagged themselves a half marathon The format will be similar this month, with guided runs led by local clubs with several running/jogging waves of a 3k route around the park. Free head torches will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. Attendees are also encouraged to wear lights and fluorescent cloth A small event village will have stalls with representatives from fitness groups, community safety organisations, and charities, and there will be food and drink vendors and music

candidates.evidence_text: Acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan is set to launch a new contemporary dining destination in Manchester this November Counter Manchester, the latest addition to the Open Restaurant Group portfolio and the first in Manchester city centre, promises to bring a ‘theatrical approach’ to dining. It follows the launch of Sheridan’s open-fire concept Arcadian in Didsbury last month The 60-cover restaurant will open in the Island Building on John Dalton Street. At its heart will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors will feature four-metre elm trees, curved boot With Counter, the award-winning chef says he wants to challenge convention by exploring what British cooking can be, placing exceptional local produce at the heart of a menu shaped by flavours, ingredients and techniques from around the world The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Football Man City Premier League charges LIVE Updated 7 mins ago Man City charges LIVE: Owners 'warned', appeal 'to drag on' despite EFL sanction stance MEN Sport brings you the latest Manchester City Premier League charges as we await the outcome of the club's appeal Add t The reigning controversy surrounding City's finances has intensified following last month's announcement that the club had been found guilty of breaching financial regulations over a nine-year period between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons According to the Premier League's findings, City inflated their reported income by more than £900million through sponsorship agreements described as 'sham' deals. The Blues have strongly rejected the allegations and formally lodged an appeal on October 1, insisting they have done In a statement responding to the decision, City maintained they were 'innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League' and insisted they had 'a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' to challenge the findings Speculation is now mounting over the potential consequences should the original ruling stand. According to the Daily Mail , the 'most likely' punishment could involve three major sanctions, including a substantial points deduction severe enough to ensure relegation and a signific Reports have also raised the possibility of further repercussions for City's ownership, with suggestions that the club's owners could face removal if the independent commission's verdict is upheld following the appeal

candidates.summary: KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI в Манчестере! 1 ноября 2026 года в Manchester Academy состоится концерт KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI в Манчестере
candidates.lead: Кавабанга Депо Колибри at Manchester Academy
candidates.practical_angle: Официальная страница должна подтверждать дату, город, площадку и старт продаж.
candidates.evidence_text: 1 ноября 2026 года в Manchester Academy состоится концерт KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI в Манчестере Манчестер — город, где встречаются культуры, музыкальные традиции и люди из разных уголков мира. Именно здесь украинское хип-хоп трио KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI снова выйдет на сцену, чтобы презентовать свою новую музыку.
